**Computational-intensive analysis of honey-derived
environmental DNA information to disclose the
effect of climate change on biodiversity**

## Research team and collaboration

These research activities were carried out within
the [Animal and Food Genomics Group](https://site.unibo.it/animal-and-food-genomics/en)
at the University of Bologna, led by
[Prof. Luca Fontanesi](https://www.unibo.it/sitoweb/luca.fontanesi/en).

My contributions are presented within this
collaborative research context.


## Project overview

eHoney explored the computational analysis
of environmental DNA recovered from honey
as a source of information on biodiversity
and environmental signatures.

The project addressed the processing and
interpretation of sequencing data to
characterize biological components
represented in honey-derived DNA.

## My research contribution

My research activities are associated with
the bioinformatic analysis and interpretation
of honey-derived environmental DNA data.

These activities connect environmental
genomics, metagenomic characterization
and computational analysis of biodiversity
information.
